p.home_lead: Jet lag is the mismatch between your body clock and the local time of the place you reach after a flight across several time zones. Sfuso takes your cities and flight times and tells you, day by day, when to sleep, when to get light and when to stop drinking coffee.

features: Light windows to seek and avoid
When to sleep on the plane

p.m_h: How the jet lag plan works
p.m_p: The plan estimates what time your body clock is at, decides whether it needs to move forward or back, and shifts it a little each day with three levers: sleep times, sunlight and coffee. In practice it tells you what to do at every hour of the trip.
p.m1_p: Your lowest body temperature falls about 2 hours before you usually wake up. It is the reference point that the rest of the plan depends on.
p.m2_h: Use light as a remote control
p.m2_p: Light in the hours after that point moves your clock earlier, light in the hours before it moves it later. Sfuso tells you which window to seek and which to avoid, every day.
p.m3_h: Shift your sleep at the right pace
p.m3_p: Your body recovers about 1 hour a day heading east and 1.5 hours heading west. The plan counts the days and takes you through to local time.
p.hd_h: How long jet lag lasts to the most popular destinations
p.hd_p: {From}, jet lag lasts from about {min_days} days for {min_city} to about {max_days} for {max_city}. Every destination has its own page with the time difference in winter and summer, a ready-made plan and the best arrival time.
p.ht_p: Four free tools for anyone who travels or works with people on the other side of the world: from the exact time in any city to the right moment for a meeting.
p.hg_h: Guides to travelling without jet lag
p.hg_p: Practical advice for the most common cases: children, overnight flights, business trips and coming home.
home_faq: How long does jet lag last?

If you do nothing, your body recovers about one hour of time difference a day, so after a flight with 6 hours' difference it takes around 6 days. With light, sleep and coffee at the right times it drops to about 1 day for every 1.5 hours heading west and 1 day per hour heading east.
Is jet lag worse heading east or west?

Heading east, for example from the UK to Japan, because you have to move your body clock earlier and go to sleep sooner, which the body does poorly. Heading west, as to New York, you just stay up later and adjustment is faster.
Is it worth adjusting to the time zone on a trip of a few days?

For a trip of 1-3 days usually not: stay on home time, schedule commitments for the hours when you would be awake at home and sleep when you would sleep at home. Sfuso has a short trip mode that shows you these hours in local time.
What is the best arrival time for jet lag?

Heading east it is best to arrive between noon and 4pm, so you avoid the early morning light that slows adjustment. Heading west, arriving around midday and staying outdoors until the evening works well. Sfuso judges your flight time and tells you how to handle it.
When should I sleep on the plane?

Sleep on the plane only during the hours when it is night at your destination. The calculator crosses your flight times with the night in the arrival city and tells you when to sleep on board. If it is daytime at your destination, it is better to stay awake or take a 20-30 minute nap.
Does melatonin help with jet lag?

Studies say melatonin helps mainly on trips heading east, taken at the time you want to fall asleep during the first days at your destination. Rules on melatonin vary from country to country, so ask your doctor or pharmacist before using it, especially if you take medication or are pregnant.
Is the calculator free, and does it save my data?

Sfuso is free and needs no sign-up. All the calculation happens in your browser: cities and flight times are not sent or saved anywhere. They stay only in the page address, so you can share the plan with a link or save it in your calendar.

t_hub_faq: Which tool should I use for a meeting abroad?

Use the meeting planner: add up to 5 cities and it colours green the hours when everyone is between 9 and 18. If there is no green, it shows you early-morning and evening hours, which are usually the least tiring compromise.
Do the tools take daylight saving into account?

Yes: they all use the official time zone database in your browser, the same one operating systems use. The differences between cities are always those of the date you choose, even in the weeks of March and October when Europe and the United States change their clocks on different days.
Do I need to sign up or install anything?
No. The tools work in your browser, including on a phone, and send no data to a server. The cities you choose are saved only on your device and in the page address, so you can share them with a link.

fusi-orari.name: Time zone converter
fusi-orari.card: What time it is in every city, with a slider to move forwards and backwards in time.
fusi-orari.title: Time zone converter: the time around the world · Sfuso
fusi-orari.desc: Free time zone converter: pick a city and a time and instantly see what time it is in the others, with daylight saving, day and time difference.
fusi-orari.lead: A time zone converter tells you what time it is in other cities when it is a certain time where you are. Choose the reference city and the time, and move the slider to see how all the others change.
text: How to use it

Choose the reference city and the time you are interested in: for example the time of a meeting. The cards show the time in the other cities, whether it is already tomorrow or still yesterday, and the difference in hours. The slider moves everything forwards or backwards half an hour at a time, useful for working out when to call someone.
Examples of differences from the UK

In winter the UK is on UTC+0 (GMT): New York is 5 hours behind and Los Angeles 8. Heading east, Dubai is 4 hours ahead, Bangkok 7, Tokyo 9 and Sydney 11. In summer (BST, UTC+1) the gaps to Dubai, Bangkok, Tokyo and Sydney shrink by an hour (3, 6, 8 and 9), because not every country uses daylight saving and those that do change their clocks on different dates.
Daylight saving is already included

Differences change during the year because countries switch to daylight saving on different dates: Europe at the end of March, the United States in mid-March, Australia in October. The converter uses the official time zone database in your browser, so the differences are always those of the date you choose.
faq: How many hours' difference are there between the UK and New York?

Usually 5 hours: when it is 12:00 in London it is 7am in New York. For a few weeks in spring and autumn the difference drops to 4 hours, because the United States and Europe change their clocks on different dates. The converter works it out for you.

riunioni.title: Meeting planner across time zones · Sfuso
riunioni.desc: Free meeting planner: add up to 5 cities and find the time when everyone is within office hours, with daylight saving and day of the week.
riunioni.lead: The meeting planner shows the 24 hours of several cities one under the other and colours green the hours when everyone is within office hours, from 9 to 18. Tap an hour to see the exact time in every city.
text: How to find the right time

The first city is the reference: the columns follow its hours. Green cells are the hours when all the cities are between 9 and 18. If there are none, as between London and Tokyo with New York, look for the orange cells: early morning for some, evening for others. It is usually the least tiring compromise.
Tips for calls across continents

Between the UK and the US East Coast the best time is early afternoon in the UK, morning in New York. With Asia, the UK morning works best, afternoon or evening for them. If someone has to join at night, alternate the time from one meeting to the next so the sacrifice is shared.
faq: What is the best time for a call between the UK and the United States?

With the East Coast, such as New York, between 2pm and 5pm UK time, which is 9am to 12pm in New York. With the West Coast, such as Los Angeles, the only comfortable window is between 4pm and 6pm UK time, early morning in California.
Are the cities I choose saved?
Yes, only on your device and in the page address: you can send the link to colleagues and they will see the same grid. No data is sent to a server.

sonno.name: Sleep calculator
sonno.card: What time to go to bed to wake up at the end of a sleep cycle.
sonno.title: Sleep calculator: what time to go to bed · Sfuso
sonno.desc: Free sleep calculator: find out what time to go to bed or set your alarm so you wake up at the end of a 90-minute sleep cycle.
sonno.lead: The sleep calculator tells you what time to go to bed, or what time to set your alarm, so you wake up at the end of a sleep cycle. Each cycle lasts 90 minutes on average and it takes about 15 minutes to fall asleep.
sonno.l_mode: What do you want to work out
sonno.l_time: I need to wake up at
sonno.hint: The darker options have 5 or 6 cycles (7.5-9 hours), the ones recommended for an adult.
text: Why wake up at the end of a cycle

Sleep moves through light, deep and REM stages that repeat roughly every 90 minutes. If your alarm goes off in deep sleep you feel groggy even after many hours; if it goes off at the end of a cycle you get up more alert. 90 minutes is an average: if you often wake a little before your alarm, your cycle is probably shorter.
Sleep and jet lag

In the first days after a flight, cycles are broken up more easily. The calculator helps you choose your alarm time, but to shift your body clock what matters most is light and regular hours: for that, use the Sfuso jet lag plan.
faq: How many hours should I sleep?

An adult needs 7-9 hours of sleep on average, that is 5 or 6 cycles of 90 minutes. Teenagers need more, 8-10 hours. A short night now and then can be made up, but regularly sleeping less than 6 hours affects attention, mood and health.
How long should a nap last?

A nap of 20-30 minutes rests you without taking you into deep sleep, so you wake up without feeling groggy. If you have time, a full 90-minute cycle works well. It is better to avoid napping after 4pm, so you do not steal sleep from the night.

ora-nel-mondo.name: World clock
ora-nel-mondo.card: The time in 16 cities and a map showing the part of the world where it is night right now.
ora-nel-mondo.title: World clock: the time right now in 16 cities · Sfuso
ora-nel-mondo.desc: What time it is right now around the world: the exact time in 16 cities with the difference from the UK and a map of where it is night at this moment.
ora-nel-mondo.h1: What time it is right now around the world
ora-nel-mondo.lead: Here you will find the exact time right now in 16 major cities, the difference from the UK and a map of the Earth showing where it is night at this moment. The line between day and night moves 15 degrees every hour.
text: How to read the map

The dark part of the map is where it is night right now. The boundary between day and night, the terminator, curves with the seasons: in summer the northern nights are short and the shadow shrinks over the northern hemisphere, in winter the opposite happens. The map updates itself while the page is open.
Time zones in numbers

There are 38 different local times in use around the world, from UTC−12 to UTC+14. China uses a single time zone for the whole country, while Russia has 11 and the United States 6 in its main territories. France, counting its overseas territories, is the country with the most time zones: 12.
Why time zones are not all a whole hour apart

Most countries use whole-hour offsets from Greenwich time, but India is on UTC+5:30, Nepal on UTC+5:45 and some Pacific islands go up to UTC+14. On top of that, daylight saving changes the differences twice a year, on different dates from country to country.
faq: What time is it in Japan right now?
Japan is 9 hours ahead of the UK in winter and 8 in summer, because Japan has no daylight saving. The exact time in Tokyo is on the card above, updated while the page is open.

UTC is Coordinated Universal Time, the reference from which all time zones are counted. The UK is on UTC+0 in winter (GMT) and UTC+1 in summer (BST), when daylight saving applies. Flight times and computer systems often use UTC to avoid confusion.

p.g_hub_title: Guides to travelling without jet lag · Sfuso
p.g_hub_desc: Practical guides to jet lag: children, overnight flights, business trips, melatonin and coffee, sunlight and coming home after a long flight.
p.g_hub_h1: Guides to travelling without jet lag
p.g_hub_lead: Practical advice for the most common cases: children, overnight flights, business trips, melatonin and coffee, sunlight and coming home. Each guide ends with the most common questions.
g_hub_faq: Which guide should I start with?

If you are leaving in a few days, start with the one on light: it is the strongest lever for shifting your body clock. If you are travelling with young children read the one on children, if you have a night flight the one on overnight flights, and before coming home the one on the return trip.
Do the guides replace medical advice?

No. The guides give general guidance based on circadian rhythm research. For supplements such as melatonin, for children, in pregnancy or if you take medication, always ask your doctor, paediatrician or pharmacist before changing your habits.
How long does a guide take to read?

Each guide is 600-750 words long, about 3-4 minutes of reading, and ends with three frequently asked questions. At the bottom you will find the link to the calculator to get a plan with the times of your flight.
